title: AI claimed a solution to the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis — and a human did, too
lede: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge released a Lean-verified proof of the Riemann hypothesis found working with Claude, while a separate all-human proof surfaced from Stanford.

points: Alpöge's proof is formalised in Lean, and mathematicians including MIT's Andrew Sutherland report that it compiles.
He released it before writing a human-readable explanation, and has committed to producing one.
Experts on Zulip are still working through the argument, which draws on deep results in automorphic forms.
Ravi Vakil posted a draft proof by postdoc Alessandro Masullo, described as entirely human and the result of 12 years of work; it is not formalised.
Alpöge and NYU's Tristan Buckmaster also released a proof related to the Navier-Stokes equations.

sections.text: Formal verification let a machine-assisted proof be checked before anyone fully understood it, which makes Lean output the bar for trusting AI-generated mathematics.
